Performed an internal review of analytics and reporting tool permissions across the CompanyOS environment to identify current access levels, potential over‑privileged accounts, and gaps in least‑privilege enforcement.

observations: Two admin accounts belong to former employees still active.
Five power_user roles have direct SQL execute privileges beyond approved query templates.
One designer role inherited admin rights via a nested group.
Audit logs show 3 instances of unauthorized data export attempts in the last 30 days.
Guest access is enabled on a public‑facing report folder, exposing aggregated sales data.
No MFA enforcement for author role despite access to sensitive KPI datasets.

recommendations: Disable or delete admin accounts for former employees and enforce a quarterly account‑review process.
Restrict power_user SQL execute rights to approved stored procedures; implement role‑based query templating.
Remove nested group inheritance that grants unintended admin privileges in the BI Dashboard Platform.
Disable guest access on internal report folders; move any public‑facing reports to a securely vetted publishing pipeline.
Enforce MFA for all roles with write or export capabilities (author, designer, power_user).
Implement automated alerting for anomalous export or data‑access patterns based on baseline usage.

risks.risk: Privilege creep leading to unauthorized data exposure
Insufficient MFA on high‑privilege roles increasing credential‑theft risk
Guest‑enabled folders leaking aggregated sensitive metrics

next_internal_actions: Run a script to list all active analytics/tool service accounts and compare against HR termination records.
Update role definitions in each tool to remove excessive privileges and document approved permission matrices.
Enable MFA enforcement policies via the identity provider for the identified high‑risk roles.
Audit guest/shared links in the reporting suite and revoke any that are not explicitly approved.
Schedule a recurring (monthly) permission review meeting with the data governance team.
Configure SIEM correlation rules to flag export actions exceeding baseline thresholds.

insights.summary: Analysis of enabling MFA enforcement policies for high-risk roles via identity provider. This is a security hardening measure targeting privileged accounts and roles with elevated access.
findings: High-risk roles typically include: domain admins, global administrators, security administrators, privileged access roles, and service accounts with elevated permissions
MFA enforcement at the identity provider level (e.g., Entra ID, Okta, Ping Identity) provides centralized control and consistent policy application
Conditional Access policies can target specific directory roles, groups, or application assignments
Current state assessment needed: existing MFA coverage, legacy authentication protocols, break-glass accounts, and service account handling
Phased rollout recommended: pilot with security team, then privileged roles, then all admin roles, with monitoring at each stage
recommendations: Inventory all high-risk roles across identity providers and linked systems
Create Conditional Access policies requiring MFA for identified roles with 'Require multifactor authentication' grant control
Configure authentication strength requirements (phishing-resistant MFA preferred: FIDO2, certificate-based auth)
Establish break-glass accounts with alternative access mechanisms (stored securely, monitored, time-limited)
Plan for service accounts: migrate to managed identities/workload identities where possible, otherwise use certificate-based auth
Enable 'Block legacy authentication' policies to prevent bypass
Configure session controls: sign-in frequency, persistent browser session limits
risks: Lockout risk if break-glass accounts not properly configured and tested
Service account disruption if not migrated before enforcement
User productivity impact during transition without proper communication and support
Legacy applications incompatible with modern auth may break
MFA fatigue attacks if only push notifications allowed (mitigate with number matching, FIDO2)
Compliance gaps if enforcement not applied to all identity providers in hybrid environments
next_internal_actions: Complete role inventory and classification across all identity providers
Design Conditional Access policy set with exclusions for break-glass accounts
Build test plan with security team pilot group
Prepare communication plan and user enablement materials
Schedule staged rollout with rollback criteria at each phase
Configure monitoring/alerting for MFA failures, lockouts, and policy exclusions
Document exception process for legitimate exclusions with time-bound reviews
